subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Fitness Literacy II: Designing a Personal Program
essentialQuestion: Can I write a program that I would actually finish?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of setting a capability goal that is specific and testable by task in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe building a weekly structure around real constraints using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving progressing safely and recognizing when to hold; correct it and explain why.
Connect adherence: what makes a program survive a bad week with reviewing and revising a program mid-cycle and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write, run, and review a six-week personal program built around a self-chosen capability goal, documenting one mid-cycle revision and its reason.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, balance, coordination, skill, or a functional task; any medical restriction is designed around with guardian input.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
